feature: The timeline ruler names the right time when zoomed in
summary: Zoomed in, every number on the ruler now sits over the moment it names, so the playhead, the gridlines and the ruler agree and a cut lined up against a number lands on it. Before, at 4x every number was drawn about three seconds left of its moment.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A recording a few minutes long makes it easiest to see.

try.do: Open a recording several minutes long and park the playhead on a round number, say 1:15.
Press 4x in the timeline's bar (or = twice with the timeline focused).
Check that the red playhead line runs down through the tick of the ruler's 1:15.
Keep pressing = until the ruler counts in tenths of a second.
Jump the playhead further along (click the scrub bar) and check the number under it is its time.
Press Fit and check the numbers are where they always were.

evaluate: At every zoom, is the number under the playhead the time the transport says?
Do the faint gridlines in the lanes start exactly at the ruler's ticks?
At Fit, does the ruler look exactly as it did before?
rough: The walk stands in for a long recording by sliding the eight second sample to the end of five minutes, so the pictures show an empty lane at 1:15; the ruler is what is under test.
The ruler still counts in plain seconds at the deepest zoom (75s, 75.2s) rather than frames, the way Premiere does; the Premiere comparison saw it and chose not to file it.
